prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: architectural game environment concept, landscape 3:2. Design an extraordinary, beautifully coherent Japanese seaside skatepark on a broad concrete pier, for the warm painterly exploration game Yorimichi. Show the ENTIRE park from a high aerial three-quarter view looking inland across it: roughly 112 by 88 metres, more than twice a small plaza, on substantial sea piers with calm blue water on three sides and an autumn forest coastline behind. A winding four-metre-wide concrete approach connects the middle of the inland edge to a country road. Buildable, believable skate architecture with generous flowing approach lanes and clear run-outs. On the west half a terraced street plaza: paired four-step and seven-step stairs, red powder-coated descending handrails, pale stone hubbas, three low manual pads, parallel low round and square flat bars, long marble ledges, mellow bank-to-bank hip and rolling speed banks. Wide street paths connect these obstacles without clutter. On the seaward east half a generous elevated sunken bowl, rounded rectangular with flowing corners, pale ivory concrete floor, muted sage transitions, a narrow terracotta tile band below the coping, wide coping deck 3 metres above pier level reached by long skateable banks. Bowl bottom is above sea level, deep walls approach true vertical at the lip for up-and-back airs, no little kicker ramps aimed out to sea. A separate open mini-ramp ribbon with opposing quarter pipes gives a gentler progression area. A clear six-metre perimeter promenade, benches, simple timber shade pergolas, a few sheltered grasses and lantern-like lamps at the edges. Beautiful restrained materials: warm chalk concrete, weathered sandy aggregate, desaturated sage, small terracotta and muted mustard accents, dark bronze perimeter railings, blue water. Crisp clean rideable surfaces, subtly rounded architectural edges; painterly low-poly game art with soft afternoon shadows, no glossy plastic, no graffiti, no branding, no crowds. Focus on elegant landform and flowing skate lines, make it feel like a destination worth exploring. No labels or UI.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: buildable architectural reference for Yorimichi's Japanese seaside skate pier, 3:2 landscape. Show a beautifully crafted street skate plaza in a low three-quarter wide view at skater eye level, with the calm sea visible through dark bronze guardrails behind. Warm chalk concrete and pale stone, red powder-coated handrails, muted terracotta stair cheeks, sparse sage-green accents; soft painterly low-poly 3D game finish in golden afternoon light, autumn Japanese coast in the distance. Clear readable skate obstacles and long smooth runways: a wide four-step staircase descending from a long 0.72m-high terrace with two straight red round handrails, an adjacent seven-step staircase at 1.26m with a pale stone hubba, and a long bank feeding both terraces. Put the obstacles side by side with 5m separation and broad landings, not crowded into one obstacle. In the foreground a 6m-long 0.22m-high rectangular manual pad with a rounded steel edge; farther along a longer 0.38m-high pad with ledges. Include one low round flat bar and one square flat bar, each on independent unobstructed 20m approach lines. Banks at the far end carry you back into these lines, with a low bank-to-bank hip in a separate lane. Surface joints flush and subtle, no holes, no random props on riding lines. Small timber shelter, benches and coastal grasses only outside the skating approaches. Composition must show obstacles from toes through tops and their approach and landing space; no cut-off foreground objects, no fisheye, no labels, no UI. Beautiful understated public-space architecture designed by people who skate.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: construction-minded bowl and transition reference for a painterly Japanese seaside skating game, wide 3:2. A clean sculpted concrete skate bowl on an elevated pier terrace overlooking calm blue sea. High oblique view shows the entire open bowl interior and perimeter deck clearly. The bowl is generous, roughly 32 by 28 metres, a rounded rectangle with big flowing corners, broad flat bottom and smooth continuously curved quarter-circle walls rising 3 metres from bottom to coping. Walls become genuinely vertical at the lip, with a short vertical section; these are UP-AND-BACK transitions for aerials landing in the same wall, not shallow ramps that launch skaters forward. Smooth tangent floor-to-wall joins, silver steel coping with only subtle protrusion, narrow terracotta tile band below the lip. Pale warm ivory floor, muted sage transition walls, sand-coloured coping deck at least 3m wide. Bottom rests above the sea; the outer bowl terrace stands above the main pier and is reached by wide long mellow banks with smooth run-ins. Beside it show a smaller opposing-quarter-pipe mini-ramp with wide flat and a gentle entry bank, as a separate progression area. Minimal dark bronze safety rail at the OUTER terrace edge well behind the coping, never across a skating line. Sparse timber benches, coastal grass planters and a simple timber pergola stay beyond landing zones. Hand-crafted low-poly architectural game render, soft matte materials, warm afternoon shadows, beautiful quiet Japanese seaside setting. Keep it a clear practical geometry reference, no people hiding the surface, no water in bowl, no pits below waterline, no graffiti, no text, no UI, no random disconnected ramps.

Use case: stylized-concept. These are actual screenshots of the current Yorimichi skate park. Redesign this specific park into a beautiful FLOWING seaside skate landscape. Produce one clear high aerial oblique architectural game concept at the same 112x88m pier scale and keep the surrounding blue sea and autumn forest game aesthetic. Diagnose visually by improving the obvious problems: currently a vast empty grey slab with isolated harsh rectangular ramps, giant raised bathtub bowl, jagged tan surface artefacts, dead vertical backs, tiny thin rails, little coherent composition. Transform the riding surfaces into connected landforms: a unified western terraced street plaza with long run-up decks, four/seven stairs, proper handrails and hubbas, banks wrapping the terraces into the flat; a central low smooth wave/hip joining lines; sweeping low perimeter return banks to keep motion circling; the eastern bowl integrated into sculpted surrounding banks instead of sheer bunker walls, connected to a southern mini-ramp through curved berms. Retain usable flatbar and manual-pad lines with long uncluttered roll-outs. Add graceful pale sand/terracotta paving bands defining the flow of the lanes and rounded landscaped islands OUTSIDE skating lines, with coastal grasses, low curved seatwalls, warm timber shade structures. Warm ivory concrete, sage riding surfaces used sparingly, terracotta edge bands, copper-red rails, rich dark timber, contrasting bronze perimeter fencing. Believable skateable geometry with tangent joins, smooth up-and-back transitions and no abrupt edges across approaches. Give the space identity through design and landform, not clutter. No annotations, arrows, labels, people, UI or photorealism. Make something far better composed than these screenshots, while achievable as clean low-poly meshes.

Use case: stylized-concept. Redesign the photographed in-game Yorimichi skate pier into a flowing, beautiful coherent public skate space. Use the screenshots as BEFORE reference only. Create a skater-eye-height wide three-quarter architectural AFTER concept, painterly low-poly game graphics. Improve the disconnected boxed-off obstacles with wraparound smooth banks, quarter-to-bank hips and rolling terrain that naturally feed a seven-stair handrail/hubba line and a separate four-stair and manual-pad line, plenty of speed/run-in/run-out. Beyond, show the elevated bowl as sculpted rolling landform with skateable outer skirts instead of blank vertical walls, with warm tile coping and real deep curved inner walls. Central smooth low rollers connect lines. Art direction: warm ivory concrete, sage-grey transitions, terracotta flowing paving ribbons and stair cheeks, red metal rails, bronze fence, dark warm timber canopy, curved low concrete seats and clustered coastal grasses kept outside skating trajectories. Subtle clean slab joints and absolutely no huge patchy tan triangle artefacts. Flowing composition with clear spaces of rest and movement; new ramps must blend tangentially into ground. Keep blue sea and autumn Japanese coast. No UI, annotations, text, crowds or graffiti. Convincing buildable shapes, not impossible intersecting ramps.
